messages:
emily: FYI I'm seeing rising Pending tiny-gpu pods in ap-southeast1-a + b since 08:00. binpacking looks weird: warm nodes idle but scheduler keeps placing on many small hosts.

raj: similar alerts here. pod spread score high despite low overall GPU usage. Could be topologySpreadConstraint + preferSpread override.

kevin: any recent scheduler config changes? I remember we flipped `topology-awareness=true` last week for AZ isolation.

emily: config shows `topology-awareness: true` and `defaultSpread: true` in scheduler-configmap. But kube-scheduler logs show constraint re-eval timeouts and falling back to spread heuristics: 
```
W0402 08:05:12.451 scheduler.go:456] topologySpread evaluation timeout, falling back to defaultSpread
```

opsbot: deploybot: scheduler v1.28.0-rc rolled to ap-southeast1 on 03/31. No other knob changes logged.

raj: also noticed CSI attach errors on some warm nodes around 07:58. snippet: `AttachVolume failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` — may cause latebind/attach churn and bounces.

kevin: Attach timeouts + spread -> scheduler avoids coalescing in same node to reduce blast radius. So we get many tiny pods across many nodes and warm nodes not reused.

emily: exact problem: warm-node label is `node.kubernetes.io/warm=true` but topologySpreadConstraint with `maxSkew=1` prevents multiple small pods landing even when same node is fine.

raj: proposed quick fix: temporarily set `defaultSpread=false` in canary region and add an admission webhook to exempt `low-priority` namespaces from topologySpread. Then revert after attach issue fixed.

kevin: +1, but let's scope: canary only ap-southeast1, and only namespaces `dev-ml`, `ci-batch`. Add a telemetry gate for NVLINK errors and attach latency.

emily: action plan: 1) patch scheduler-configmap canary -> defaultSpread=false 2) create webhook exemption for low-priority namespaces 3) run targeted descheduler with preferPack=true for those namespaces (dry-run first) 4) investigate CSI attach timeouts (ops to open ticket).

oncall-bot: ack will patch canary config in 5m. Also will run a dry-run descheduler job.

srebot: opened ticket SRE-3242: CSI attach RPC deadlines increased from 20s->120s for investigation. Assigned to kevin.

kevin: bumping CSI timeout temporarily may reduce attach failures—will test on canary nodes.

raj: I'm worried about collateral: coalescing may increase per-node GPU memory contention for jobs expecting isolation. Add p95 tail latency guard (if >12% increase rollback).

emily: agreed. I'll wire up `infra-kpis` monitor for p95 inference latency and GPU temp/NVLINK error rate.

opsbot: scheduler-configmap patched in canary at 08:12. `defaultSpread=false` applied.

emily: dry-run descheduler returned 28 candidate evicts in `dev-ml` and `ci-batch`. Will run live in waves of 10.

kevin: CSI timeout bump applied to canary node kubelet at 08:20. Monitoring attach success.

oncall-bot: eviction wave 1 run at 08:25: 10 pods evicted -> 9 rescheduled to 3 warm nodes.

emily: p95 token latency +3% so far, NVLINK errors zero. GPU util on warm nodes climbed 33%->61%.

raj: eviction rate normalized, Pending count dropped by 60%. Looks promising.

kevin: attach success rate on canary improved from 86%->98% after timeout bump. We'll continue to monitor.

emily: next steps: file post-action to revert scheduler defaultSpread after CSI root cause fixed; add e2e test ensuring warm-node label + topologySpreadConstraint interact as expected; update runbook.

raj: I'll draft a short PR to add an exemption annotation `scheduler.redwood/allow-coalesce` and tests.

kevin: SRE-3242 will track CSI root cause; plan to revert kubelet timeout change after root cause fixes.

emily: thanks. closing short incident in 24h if metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
